utterances.text: Yes, in my earlier statements I didn't provide all of the details because a lot of time was needed for that. Later on I went through my statement, earlier statement, and provided additional details.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. As you were preparing to testify here, did Mr. McCloskey show to you all of the statements mentioned so far? Did you have occasion to see all of them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-111 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And you had certain comments and corrections pertaining to the statement given to Mr. Ruez, namely, that some of the things you said to him were not fully accurate, and you enumerated those facts, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-111 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There were not a lot of mistakes, but some minor typing mistakes or translation mistakes, minor mistakes that I corrected.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. In addition to these corrections that you pointed out during your proofing, there were no additional significant corrections that you wanted to make in relation to your previous statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-111 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now I would like to get to the essence of your evidence. In the course of your testimony yesterday, you said that you set out from the village of Jaglici with a column heading towards Tuzla. This village of Jaglici is at the very outskirts of the Srebrenica enclave, and this is where the UNPROFOR check-point was, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-111 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And as soon as you passed by the UNPROFOR check-point, you and other men in the column found yourselves in the territory which was under the control of the army of Republika Srpska from 1993, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-111 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And it was outside of the borders of the enclave of Srebrenica, as it was defined before its fall in 1995, this territory where you found yourself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-111 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday you told the Prosecutor that, as you can best remember, you set on the 20th of July -- on the 12th of July in the afternoon with the other men. Is this a precise date, according to your best recollection?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-111 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, on the 11th I left Srebrenica, and I arrived at Jaglici on the 12th, in the morning at dawn. On the 12th, in the afternoon, together with the other men in the column, I set off towards Tuzla through the woods.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. About the movement of people, we know that things more or less proceeded with women, the elderly and children going off towards Potocari, the men going towards Tuzla through the woods, that that's how things happened. But do you happen to have any information about a number of wounded trying, over those few days, on the 12th or the 13th, trying to enter the UNPROFOR base in Potocari but that the DutchBat members did not permit that? Are you aware of that, perhaps?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-111 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know. I wasn't in Potocari, and I don't know what was happening. I know that the women, children and the elderly were exhausted and were going towards Potocari to the UNPROFOR compound. But I don't know what else happened that day, because I went through the woods to Jaglici.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: All right. Well, if you don't know, that is quite all right. If you don't know something, please feel free to say so, and then that will make this cross-examination much shorter. During your testimony yesterday, you replied to a question by my learned friend, Mr. McCloskey, that you are a member of the B and H army; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-111 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Other than you, the -- there was a large number of members of the B and H army in this column that was going to Jaglici, not just you, and mostly they were able-bodied men of that age?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-111 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: When I was reading your prior statements I found information that you personally were not armed, that you had never been issued a weapon, but only when you went to the line were you then able to take a rifle from another soldier who was already there and when you -- your shift was completed, then you would give your rifle to another soldier. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-111 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The column that went from Jaglici to Tuzla contained a substantial number of people who did have weapons, hunting weapons and other types of weapons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-111 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So just to continue in this topic, you also said that you belonged to the 272nd [as interpreted] Brigade, which was part of the 28th Division; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Witness, you need to answer yes or no, because otherwise -- I saw you nodding, but the interpreters need to hear you answer yes or no.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I said yes. Perhaps they didn't hear me. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The witness did say but there was some overlapping, unfortunately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I didn't hear it. Yes, please, try to slow down because this is creating problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. I want to make one correction in the transcript, on page 50, line 9, it says "272nd Brigade". It's 282nd Brigade. And the Witness confirmed it, so...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, 282nd.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And the commander of the 282nd Brigade was Ibro Dudic who had the rank of major at the time. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-111 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about his rank. Dudic Ibro was my commander however, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Just a couple more things about this. Your membership of the 282nd Brigade, I just wanted to clarify something about that. Were you just a regular soldier or did you have any kind of command function? Well, starting from being a regular soldier, then we have other ranks, privates and so on, lance corporal, so could you please tell us what your rank was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-111 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was just a regular soldier.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: As part of the 282nd Brigade, there were some smaller units. Could you please -- do you know which of those smaller units you belonged to, that was part of the 282nd Brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-111 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I have forgotten a lot of things, so I really don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Perhaps we can clarify some of those things when I show you certain documents. Could you please help us to identify what they mean, what is the meaning of certain abbreviations, and can you please tell me before I show you that document, as far as I understood you during your JNA service, were in the anti-aircraft defence; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-111 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I believe we should move into private session because the name of the witness is mentioned in the document, and then I will ask for these documents to be shown to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Let's move into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We have finished with this document. You have helped as much as you could. I would now like to move to the topic of the column's break through towards Tuzla from Jaglici. The column went in the direction of Ravni Buljim; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-111 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Talking -- actually, in your testimony in the Krstic case before this Tribunal, and I can tell my learned friends from the Prosecution exactly which page and which line it is from the transcript from over there, and if I remember, you said the following: [In English] [Previous translation continues] ... with the uniform." Okay. I apologise. I will quote again. "I never put on a uniform. I was never issued with a uniform."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-111 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, that I never was.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And also in the Krstic case, a little bit after that, you said the following, speaking about weapons and the people in the column who were armed. "[In English] [Previous translation continues] ... had thrown them away in the woods." Well, I will start again. "Those who had weapons had thrown them away in the woods. We did not dare surrender with weapons." [Interpretation] So you didn't have weapons, but we are talking about those in the column who did have weapons at the time of surrender. Do you stand by what you said, that they had thrown away their weapons in the woods before they surrendered?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-111 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And the reason why they threw away their weapons was that they did not want Serb soldiers to find out that soldiers of the B and H army were involved. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-111 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And of course they wanted to present themselves as civilians when they were surrendering?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-111 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most probably, yes. Even though they knew that people had weapons. Not all, but some did.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I would now like to show you another thing. This part of your testimony went quite quickly during the examination-in-chief by Mr. McCloskey. While attempting to break through, and before surrendering, you said that at one point there was some exchange of fire between the column on one side and you said there "Chetniks." Do you remember where, roughly, this exchange of fire took place between the column and the Chetniks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-111 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We came up against one ambush, actually there were more, there was more than one ambush, people are driven away. Everything gets quiet, they rejoin the column, and you just continue on the way.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I completely agree with you. I completely agree with you. There were a substantial number of witnesses who also left in the column like you did and said that there were attacks on the column, that the column had broken up, reassembled and so on and so forth. What I am interested in, the specific situation when there was an exchange of fire, according to my understanding of your statement, that should have happened on the 13th, early, at dawn. Did this happen soon after you left on the 13th at dawn?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-111 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this was before. It was night. I don't know exactly what time of the night, what time it was. I don't know, but it was during the night. We came up on an ambush near Kravica. It was near the place where I had come down to the asphalt to surrender together with the other people. That's where we came up on an ambush. Many dead and wounded were left there. There was shooting, hand-grenades were thrown. They were firing from the asphalt. They were firing anti-aircraft guns from tanks, they were throwing hand-grenades into the woods where we were.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: All right. But you know why I'm asking you all of this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Please stop, Mr. Lazarevic, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey and Mr. Lazarevic, it is our opinion that this latter part, which -- of Mr. Lazarevic's cross-examination which has taken some time basically deals with events that it is our understanding you have already conceded. Namely, that indeed there was a column consisting of, to an extent, armed Muslims and that there were shoot-outs. Am I correct or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Absolutely, Mr. President. And he's also testified that there were hundreds of dead in that area as well. And...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So perhaps you can take it as already conceded by the Prosecution and move to what perhaps is more relevant to your client.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I will do this in due course. My main -- well, to be honest, Your Honours, I frankly not -- I'm not quite sure what Mr. McCloskey is stipulating. We are in -- in the process of preparation of certain -- well, agreed facts. We discussed this among the Defences for quite some period, and we will proceed with -- with proposing certain -- certain facts which are agreed by the Defence to the Prosecution, and if we manage to do so, then there will be no more examination on this topic. However, whether this was a military column from the very beginning and whether it was a legitimate military target, if this is something that the Prosecution is ready to stipulate, then we are very close to get this -- this agreed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Do you wish to comment on that, Mr. McCloskey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I have no problem discussing this. I prefer not to discuss it in front of the witness. And it -- I can point out, it is not a subject matter of the indictment, and I think that's pretty clear. And I -- I -- a lot of this I can -- I think I already have agreed to informally. But I don't -- I don't -- I don't think it's a good idea to talk too much detail in front of witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I'm fine with what my colleague said. I was about to leave this topic anyway.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. So let's leave it and move...

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Witness, when you went on the break-through from Jaglici, I found this bit of information in your evidence in Sarajevo. You had on you your passport and your ID card, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-111 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did have my passport. I don't remember having my ID.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: But at any rate, you discarded the ID that you had, whichever one of the two you had, while you were in the forest, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-111 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Did you notice that other people in the column were getting rid of their IDs before they decided to go down to the road and surrender?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-111 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now, let us summarise this, please. If I were to tell you now you were a member of the BH Army, but at the moment when you surrendered you did not have your uniform, you did not have your ID, and you did not have your weapon. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-111 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And all of that was done in order to avoid being identified as a soldier of the BH Army, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-111 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not what I was afraid of. They naturally asked me once I came down to the asphalt road, or rather, had they asked me about my first name and last name, I would have told them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you explain to us why you discarded your documents if you were prepared to give your full name anyway?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-111 [Resumed]
utterances.text: To tell you the truth, I don't know. I threw my ID away in order not to have anything on me. I didn't want to have any document on me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Now, let us turn to the moment after your surrender on the asphalt road when you reached the meadow. In the statement you gave to the OTP on the 3rd of December, you said that there were a number of wounded men there who were taken to nearby houses, some distance away from where you were sitting, and the reason for that was that the wounded needed to be taken out of the sun, because it was quite hot on that day. And you stated something similar yesterday.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-111 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: On page 18 of the Sarajevo transcript, you said that this moving of the wounded from the meadow to this house was done at the request of the prisoners. Correct? Namely that you, I don't mean you personally, but other captives there, asked the Serb soldiers to move the wounded away, so that they wouldn't lie there in the sun and that they said yes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-111 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not true. I have to say this: The Serb soldiers saw that the wounded were fainting, and that people from my group had to constantly go and fetch water nearby in order to cool and refresh the wounded. So they decided themselves to take the wounded to this -- to these two houses nearby, to move them out of the sun.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I'm not denying that that happened, I'm just interested in learning whether this was done at the initiative of you, the prisoners, or them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-111 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they did it on their own.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: While you were there in the meadow, did you perhaps see whether there were any women treating or assisting the wounded?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-111 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: All right. During your evidence yesterday, you said that women, girls and those who were below the age of 18, on the meadow in Sandici, were allowed to board the bus and go to Tuzla. You said that they said whoever is younger than 18 can step out and will be evacuated. Do you remember this portion of your testimony?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-111 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Did you say anything, Mr. Lazarevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I apologise. I said that we should move into private session for a -- one very -- question. I apologise for this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-111 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We will certainly get to other details later. When testifying here you didn't mention something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's go into private session for a short while.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. We will have a break very soon, Mr. Lazarevic. So any time it's suitable for you, we can go into break.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, I cannot finish with this topic in two minutes. Maybe we can take the break now and continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go ahead. Do you wish to take the break now? Because if you do, we'll take the break now.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: It will be okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. So in the meantime, let me sign the redaction, please. And we will reconvene in 25 minutes' time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, we are still on the meadow in Sandici. I will try to cover that as quickly as possible. There is a detail that appears in your earlier testimony that you failed to mention here, and that is the water tank on -- in the Krstic case you spoke about this water truck arriving, and spraying water on you three times. Do you remember this incident with the water truck?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-111 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Now, in relation to that, can you remember what colour that truck was? Was it a red fire water truck or a green one?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-111 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the red fire brigade water truck with a water gun that sprayed water under pressure, and they sprayed the water on us.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I don't know if you can remember this, but do you know from which direction the water truck came, from Konjevic Polje or Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-111 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see that, I only saw it arriving on the meadow, but I didn't notice the direction that it had come from.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: All right. When testifying in the Mitrovic et al case in Sarajevo, you said that this spraying with water refreshed you, it cooled you down in that heat. You still stand by that statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-111 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey, could you read the last -- line 6, 7 and 8?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, and that's -- I know we're going back to that other case, and we should probably try to stay away from that, but...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Let's -- let's move.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, maybe we should establish some practice because I do intend to use more of these transcripts from Sarajevo. Maybe I can quote to the witness without mentioning day and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Or we can go in private session if you are going to be particular. Because --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: That is also a solution. I will try to avoid going into private session. This is not the policy of Tribunal to try to use it as less as possible, but basically I can do it this way, if that's Your Honour's position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I would prefer if we stick to the practice of taking him to the place that you're asking them about in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What I suggest is that you put direct questions to the witness relating to the facts without necessarily referring to and then if you are not satisfied with the answer, you can confront him with previous testimony or previous statements. And then we will see whether we go into private session or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I will follow this order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I mean, just to give you an example, I mean, the last question you could have asked him, "Would it be correct if I put it to you that when you were sprayed with the water, this you considered to be kind of a refreshment for you in that heat?" And if he says "yes", you are happy with the answer. If he says "no," you can of course confront him with a previous statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour is right, however sometimes it is my strategy to face him directly with something he previously said and ask him whether he can confirm or not. That's also one way of cross-examining the witness. I feel much better with this way. But I will try to avoid any misunderstanding between --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: -- us and...

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yesterday, in your evidence in relation to the meadow in Sandici, you said that there were approximately between 1.500 and 2.000 prisoners there. Remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-111 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Now I would like to look at a photograph. According to the Prosecution case, this photograph was an aerial photograph taken on the 13th of July, 1995 at about 1400 hours. Which means that, according to your description of events, you should have been at the meadow in Sandici at that time. [In English] 4DP01579. Okay. If we can zoom this, and -- yeah, I think so. [Interpretation] Please look at this. If needed, we can enlarge it so that you can see it better. Do you see the road, the meandering road and the buses on the road?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-111 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: To the lower portion in relation to the buses, there is a black rectangle. Do you see it? According to the Prosecution case, this depicts those -- the prisoners in the meadow in Sandici at 1400 hours. Do you see that? Can you tell what this is about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-111 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could we zoom in, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you see it better now? It's precisely what we need. You see the buses, and immediately below the buses there is something resembling a rectangle.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-111 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Looking at this photograph, would you agree with me that judging by the dimensions and comparing them -- comparing them to the dimension of the buses, that the figure could not be between 1.500 and 2.000, that it should be a much lower figure? I know that you didn't count how many people there were there, but talking about your assessment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection. Two grounds. One, the figure that was given by the witness was not based at a particular time, as my recollection was, it was more of a total figure. And to ask a witness to evaluate an image like this, based on buses out of the -- is really asking for speculation and not appropriate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can understand the objection of Mr. McCloskey. However, the witness made some estimation during his testimony. He never gave exact numbers; he said it was my estimation based on -- well, Mr. McCloskey never actually established what were the bases for his estimation. On the other hand, this is in the time-frame of the indictment, so I believe I am perfectly entitled to ask the witness this question. If he knows, he can agree with me, that's fine. And he doesn't --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think he has now heard submissions from both sides, so I don't think I should labour the point much further. However, there is one thing that needs to be clarified. When previously you said there were in the region of 1.500 to 2.000, were you referring to any specific time? What were you referring at? How did you come to that conclusion? When was it that you think there were 1.500 or 2.000 Muslims gathered there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I arrived with the first group. Following me, after some time, after perhaps half an hour or an hour, I'm not quite sure, another group arrived at the meadow. Another column enjoined the group where I was. I recognised two men at the helm of the column; there were two brothers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't want these details. When you arrived there, how many Muslims do you reckon were already there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We were the first to arrive there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So how many of you were there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] About 1.000, perhaps 1.500. I'm not quite sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And when the second group arrived?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Then the number increased. 1.500 to 2.000, maybe even more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And how long after you had arrived did the second group arrive?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just said a bit earlier, perhaps half an hour to an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I know you did, but I just want to put everything in just one scenario now. Yes, Mr. Lazarevic. You can ask him the question, and if he can answer it, he will. If he cannot answer it, then we will see.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: That's okay. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, if you remember, my question was that when you look at this now, do you think that this number from 1.500 to 2.000 is a little bit exaggerated when you look at this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-111 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see any people on this photograph at all. And this is not a place that I'm familiar with. I cannot recognise the place.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, that's understandable. I'm not going to insist on that. But however, responding today to His Honour, the Presiding Judge's question, you said that the first group that you surrendered with came to the meadow in Sandici first and that it numbered between 1.500 to 2.000 people. However, when you replied to the same question in the Sarajevo case, which is on page 18 -- [In English] Well, maybe we should move into private session right now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's move into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We could call it the southern site.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Witness, you know which site we are referring to; you have heard us. So, please, don't repeat the site again. Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The southern location, in reply to the same question, you said that in this first group that you surrendered in, you said there were 15 to 20 wounded and that there were between three to 500 of you in total. Do you recall that? This is easy to check, and my learned friends from the Prosecution have that transcript.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-111 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall saying that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: All right. I'm not going to insist further. In your testimony in the Krstic case, and in your other testimony, and speaking in general about the events at the Sandici meadow, you talked about the soldiers who were guarding you and so on and so forth. I would like you now to help me with your answer. Did I understand correctly, there was a group of soldiers that was there when you surrendered, and this group was guarding you. There was another group of soldiers who came at one point in black uniforms and it is your position more or less that these soldiers who guarded you first treated you properly, whereas these other soldiers in black uniforms were people who were arrogant and who, according to your testimony, killed one of the prisoners. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-111 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And your conclusion was that these were two different units; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-111 [Resumed]
utterances.text: How should I know what unit that was and who the people in black uniforms were? Those who were guarding us, nobody touched us, they didn't beat us, they spoke to us normally, they knew some people from Skelani, there were some Serbian soldiers who knew these other people who came in this other column. Ahmo and his brother Dzemo who were walking at the front of the column, they took them aside to the tank, they talked to them. They said, "Where are you neighbours?" So I concluded that they knew each other from Skelani.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: My question was if, according to your understanding, these were two different units, one in black uniforms and the other one in the camouflage uniforms, that was my question.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-111 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The killing of one of the prisoners at the meadow which you described yesterday in your testimony was carried out by a member of the unit that had the black uniforms; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-111 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. During your testimony in the Krstic case, and you testified about that yesterday too, you said that together with Mladic, when he came to the meadow, there was a cameraman who filmed you, and specifically in the Krstic case, it is said that he was wearing a military uniform. Also in your statement to Mr. Ruez, you said this was a soldier who wore a short-sleeved T-shirt, this cameraman who was filming. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-111 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall saying that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: All right. Very well. Do you rule out that it was like that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-111 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was a cameraman who was filming but I don't remember a uniform that he was wearing. I don't know if he had a military uniform on or if he was wearing civilian clothes. There was also a photograph who was taking pictures.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: All right. Well, it's quite understandable that you cannot remember that now. Can you please tell us, at one point when the buses came to the meadow, do you remember from which direction the two buses came that you mentioned yesterday?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-111 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The bus that took you to the Kravica warehouse, the two buses that came to collect you, which direction did they come from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-111 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And do you remember approximately what time it was when you boarded the buses and left the meadow to go to Kravica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-111 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was sometime in the afternoon. It was still sunny; it was very hot.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you very much. Do you remember if there were some Serbian soldiers in the buses who were there until you got to Kravica, but then when I looked at your previous statements, I concluded that you were not able to identify these as soldiers who had guarded you at Kravica or were they someone else, that you didn't actually see the soldiers who were in the buses until you actually got to Kravica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-111 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were a couple of them escorting, but I didn't see which soldiers they were, whether they were from the meadow or some other soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is precisely how I understood your previous answer, so I just wanted to make sure that that was so. In your testimony to date, you said that you were the first to enter the Kravica warehouse, that no one else was inside and that you were practically the first group to come there. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-111 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: In regard to the events in Kravica, I think that there were some things that were a little bit unclear during your testimony. You were constantly asked questions about the firing, the shooting. Well, let's proceed like this. I'm going to be putting questions to you, but let us keep two things in mind. If I understood you correctly, there is firing that took place outside; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-111 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And then there is the other firing where this soldier comes and opens fire at you who were inside the warehouse. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-111 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let us --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Please slow down a little bit. Allow a short pause between question and answer, because the interpreters are finding it difficult to catch up with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I would now like to try to be as specific as possible about establishing the chronology. Now, you come to Kravica, you entered the hangar, then another group comes that also enters the hangar, and the hangar starts to get filled with people. What I have said now, was that how it was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-111 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: After that a Serb civilian comes who gives you cigarettes and they take the rest of your property, gold, watches, as you said, and a list was made of all the things that you handed over. Of course this happened after you arrived there. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-111 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: After that event, some time passes, you are still inside, some people bring water, but nothing significant happens other than some soldiers coming, asking about their own. They asked two of your colleagues, prisoners, there you showed on the wall where they were interrogated but they didn't beat them, they didn't mistreat them and then they are returned to you. Is that the sequence of events? Is that correct the way I have just told it right now?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-111 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, people didn't bring water, but Serb soldiers brought water.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Perhaps I was not precise enough, but thank you for that correction.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-111 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic, I just want to know whether we are going to go through his testimony part by part and ask him to confirm it again.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: No, I will just have a couple of key points which I believe are not -- well, particularly precisely explained because I believe that there was some confusion and then I will move to...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Just one question has come to me, listening to your testimony today. In that photograph that you marked, when you marked in the wire fence -- do you recall marking that wire fence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-111 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: That was a fence made of wire through which you could see what was going on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-111 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that was all that I was interested in. You were able to have a view through the fence out towards the passage in front of you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-111 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let's go back to the events now. Serb soldiers were bringing in water. At one point you could hear shooting from outside and you don't know what happened there. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-111 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: After the shooting, Serb soldiers come inside and then they're angry after what happened outside. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-111 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they were angry before.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Again, I mean, I don't think this needs clarification because this line of questioning was put already by Mr. McCloskey, and we had clear answers, repeated also, that they were angry before, and they were also angry afterwards. I mean, I think it's clear. So why are we beating the same --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can understand that, but maybe if we take a look at some other documents, then maybe it will change the opinion, but all right, I'll come to this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Then go to the other documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And then when you say they came and they were angry, that was the time that they wanted to fire at you, but that young man prevented them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-111 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't hear you very well. Can you please say that again?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: After the shooting outside that you did not see, Serb soldiers entered and they wanted to shoot at you, but one of them said, "Don't, they are not to blame for anything." Is that when this happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-111 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, before that. Not then. I already described what happened before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He has already given a description also of the time that this happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: This happened while it was still day; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-111 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The episode in which the soldier that you described came with the glasses, the long hair and the beard and who fired at you, happened when it was already dark, when it was already getting dark. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-111 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So between these two events, the first one when you had the firing outside, and this second event where the soldier comes in and fires at the prisoners, there was some time that passed. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-111 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That soldier fired into the people -- at us after the shooting outside.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Precisely, that is my question. How much time passed between those two events, between the shooting outside and the shooting that took place when the soldier fired at you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-111 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that in a previous statement I said that, but I will say that again. It's no problem. About half an hour passed between those two events.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: But this second shooting incident happened sometime around 9.00 in the evening, according to your estimate. This is in several of your statements. Somewhere it's even at 9.30. I think you told that to Mr. Ruez, that the firing started after it was already dark at around 9.00, the second firing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-111 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first one was -- it happened when you could still see, and it wasn't quite dark, but it was getting dark and then half an hour later, I don't know 100 per cent I said that, roughly, I mean I didn't have a watch to measure the time in the panic and the fear. It was getting dark. They opened fire at us. The first two soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I understand you really well, but I just wanted to clarify that. Of course you didn't look at the watch and all of that is all right. But you concluded that it was around 8.30 or 9.00 on the basis of the fact that it was beginning to get dark, and since it was mid-July when the days are pretty long, you decided on the basis of that that was the time that this thing was taking place in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-111 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. The daylight is longer in the summer.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. [In English] Your Honours, can we move into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are in open session, so let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: But you did not receive any official order or any decision from your commanders or any authorities about not being a soldier any longer? Nobody in Srebrenica gave you any official document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-111 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, nobody gave me anything. It's just that an order came for us to flee from Srebrenica, which means that the army ceased to exist. People fled wherever they could.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let me put another question to you about the evacuation. In your earlier evidence, you said that you were able to leave the UN compound to see the evacuation of women and children leaving Zepa?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-111 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And this evacuation was monitored by the International Red Cross?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-111 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The International Red Cross was within the UNPROFOR compound, only there. Now, as to whether they monitored the evacuation, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [In English] [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Sir, you said that when being evacuated from Zepa, there were UNPROFOR members on the bus with you, namely, French and Ukrainian soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-111 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Were they present on other buses? Were there escorts on other buses as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-111 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. I don't have any further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Krgovic. Who is next? Will you finish in three minutes, Madam Fauveau?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. I don't think we need it at this point in time. We need to adjourn basically. She will need much more than three minutes. Witness, you need to return again tomorrow morning so that we go -- we proceed with your testimony and hopefully finish it. We stand adjourned until tomorrow morning at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 8th day of February, 2007, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.43 p.m.,
